basis: Hereditary susceptibility specifically targets CNS glioma; susceptibility does not establish an existing tumour or additional organ damage.
Thymic epithelial origin is outside the axes. Lung/liver metastases reported in ~30% collectively do not establish that frequency for either organ.
Defining arthrogryposis, renal tubulopathy and cholestasis; ichthyosis occurs in roughly half of ARC cases. Variable platelet and CNS abnormalities omitted.
Hyperostosis causes cranial neuropathy and hearing loss in most; visual loss/optic atrophy meets the supplied frequency evidence. Nail and dental abnormalities omitted at cap.
Inherited marrow failure; absent thumbs in 2/4 and absent radii in 1/3 support common skeletal defects. Pigment macules alone do not establish skin damage.
Malignant tumour arising in lung; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish disease of skeletal muscle or bone.
Defining cerebellar/brainstem malformation and developmental impairment; retinopathy in 1/2. Renal pelvic dilation in 1/2 does not establish renal injury or dysfunction.
Suprasellar meningeal tumour; optic nerve compression with visual impairment occurs in most patients (~70–90%). Endocrine dysfunction is less common.
Defining gonadotropin deficiency; persistent anosmia/hyposmia in 3/8 (~38%) supports olfactory dysfunction. Dental agenesis in 2/8 is below threshold.
Congenital enlargement of the cornea; an isolated ocular structural disorder.
Corticospinal and cerebral white-matter disease with intellectual disability. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; delayed puberty alone does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Immune-mediated demyelinating polyneuropathy. Ophthalmoplegia reflects cranial neuropathy; paraprotein/cold antibodies alone do not establish blood-cell damage.
Malignancy of T lymphocytes in marrow and blood. Leukemia alone does not meet the infection, autoimmunity or lymphoma mechanism criteria.
Sparse concept suggests a skeletal growth disorder. Bluish sclerae alone do not establish ocular dysfunction; no definition or phenotype frequencies are supplied.
Malignant neoplasm of the retina. Lymphoma is only one subtype and does not justify an immune label for the umbrella.
Inherited organelle dysfunction; albinism or palmoplantar keratoderma affects most major subtypes (>30%). Bleeding, immune and neurologic defects vary across the group.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; conductive hearing loss is common across major OPD/frontometaphyseal forms (~30%+ overall). Cleft palate varies substantially by subtype.
Thyroid gland overproduction of thyroid hormones. Tachycardia is a functional sign; atrial fibrillation and osteoporosis are separately diagnosed complications.
Hereditary mixed intestinal polyposis directly affects colorectal mucosa; subsequent cancer risk does not add another organ.
Inherited hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, sometimes with ventricular noncompaction; disease is defined by myocardial abnormalities.
Tumour arises in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes. Rhabdomyoblastic differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Defined ocular movement disorder with nystagmus. Associated head nodding and torticollis do not establish structural neurologic or musculoskeletal damage.
Benign neoplasm arising within the CNS; smooth-muscle histology does not change its organ of origin.
Structural deformity of the foot with collapse of the longitudinal arch.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual disability in 11/13. Asthma in 4/13 is a separately diagnosed disease; skeletal findings individually occur in <30%.
